title: The target: exam, blueprint, sponsorship, clocks, and reading the stem

reading.body:
The Series 7 is a **job license, not a diploma**. It qualifies you as a General Securities Representative. That person may solicit and take securities orders for customers. The license is a work permit, so **a FINRA member firm must sponsor you**. You cannot sign up on your own.

The Series 7 has a co-requisite, the **SIE (Securities Industry Essentials)**. Co-requisite means either order works, but you need both to register. The SIE needs no sponsor, and you can take it at 18. So most people pass the SIE first. They use it to land the job that then sponsors the Series 7.

The exam is built from four Functions. Learn the item counts. **F1, Seeks Business:** 9 items, 7%. **F2, Opens Accounts:** 11 items, 9%. **F3, Provides Information, Makes Recommendations, Transfers Assets, Keeps Records:** 91 items, 73%. **F4, Processes Transactions, including margin:** 14 items, 11%.

The most important planning fact is the **73/27 rule**. Function 3 is 91 of 125 scored questions. Every product, all the math, all the tax treatment, and every suitability question lives in F3. The math means yields, options profit and loss, accrued interest, and TEY. A study plan that splits time evenly across the four Functions spends 75% of its effort on 27% of the exam. That is the top reason people fail.

reading.h: The numbers you sit down to
reading.body:
Learn the **Series 7** numbers first. It has 125 scored questions plus **5 unscored pretest** questions, so **130 items** total. You get **3 hours 45 minutes**, which is 225 minutes. The passing score is **72**, equated, and the fee is **$395** in 2026, flat through 2029. Questions are four-option multiple choice with one best answer. There is **no penalty for guessing**, so answer everything.

The **SIE** is smaller: 75 scored plus 5 pretest = 80 items, 1 hour 45 minutes, passing score **70**, fee **$100**, valid **4 years**.

Watch for stale numbers. Older prep material says '10 pretest, 135 total'. That is the pre-2018 format and is wrong. Use 130. The test center gives you a **four-function calculator** and erasable boards. There is no TVM calculator.

Scores are **equated**. Different candidates get slightly different question sets. A statistical adjustment puts everyone on one 0 to 100 scale, so no one is punished for drawing a harder form. This means **'72% = 90 of 125' is only an approximation**. Aim for about **85% raw** so the equating adjustment never matters.

**If you pass, you see only the word Pass, never a number.** If you fail, the report shows your equated score plus a profile split by the four Functions. You build a retake plan from that profile. You can never review the questions, and results are final.

reading.h: Sponsorship, Form U4, and the 120-day window
reading.body:
To sit the Series 7, a firm files **Form U4** through **CRD**. CRD is the Central Registration Depository, FINRA's database of licensed people. The U4 collects your employment history, home addresses, and disclosure answers. It requires **fingerprinting** and opens a **120-day exam window**. You must schedule within that window. If it expires, the firm files again and pays again.

The SIE needs nothing but a FINRA account and a credit card. That gap is the whole strategy. Pass the SIE without a sponsor to make yourself a low-risk hire. Then let the employer file the U4.

reading.h: The four clocks after you pass
reading.body:
Four clocks start when you pass. Put them on one timeline.

**SIE validity is 4 years** from the pass date.

**The registration lapse is 2 years.** If you leave the industry and stay unregistered for 2 years or more, you must re-qualify by exam under Rule 1210.08.

**The MQP runs up to 5 years.** The Maintaining Qualifications Program lets you park a qualification for up to 5 years by doing annual CE. You must elect it within 2 years of termination and have been registered at least 1 year.

**Continuing Education is due every December 31.** The Regulatory Element is due each year by year-end. The Firm Element is an annual training plan the firm designs.

Most missed questions are misread, not unknown. Use the same steps on every item.

**First, find the polarity word.** Circle EXCEPT, NOT, LEAST, MOST, or BEST before you read the options. An EXCEPT question asks for the one **false** choice.

**Second, find the verb.** Ask whether the question wants what is permitted, required, or recommended.

**Third, triage the data.** Scenario stems bury two or three facts that do not matter. Only a couple decide the answer.

**Fourth, strike the two impossible options.** Then choose between the last two. Most items give you four choices, and two are easy to drop. The exam lives in the choice between the last two.

Series 7 = 72; SIE = 70. Both equated on a 0–100 scale.

flashcards.front: What does 'equated' mean for your target?
flashcards.back: A statistical adjustment levels different forms, so '72% = 90 of 125' is only approximate. Aim for about 85% raw.

flashcards.front: What score do you see if you pass?
flashcards.back: None. You see only 'Pass'. A fail shows the equated score plus a profile split by Function.

flashcards.front: Who can sit the Series 7 vs the SIE?
flashcards.back: Series 7 needs a FINRA member firm to sponsor you via Form U4 (120-day window). The SIE needs no sponsor, minimum age 18.
SIE 4 years; 2-year unregistered lapse (re-exam); MQP up to 5 years; CE Regulatory Element by December 31 each year.

flashcards.front: Penalty for guessing on the Series 7?

flashcards.back: Polarity word (EXCEPT/NOT/LEAST/MOST/BEST) → verb → triage data → strike two → choose between the last two.

quiz.stem: Which Function accounts for the largest share of the Series 7 exam?
options: Function 1 — Seeks Business (9 items)
Function 2 — Opens Accounts (11 items)
Function 3 — Provides Information and Makes Recommendations (91 items)
Function 4 — Processes Transactions (14 items)
quiz.explanation: Function 3 is 91 of 125 scored questions (73%) — the 73/27 rule. It holds every product, all the math, tax, and suitability. F4 (14 items) is where margin and settlement live but is far smaller.

quiz.stem: How many questions does a Series 7 candidate answer, and how many are scored?
options: 135 total, 125 scored
130 total, 125 scored
130 total, 120 scored
125 total, all scored
quiz.explanation: The current (post-2025 outline) exam is 125 scored + 5 unidentified pretest = 130 items. '135 total / 10 pretest' is the stale pre-2018 figure still printed in some prep material.

quiz.stem: A candidate passes the Series 7. What score information does the candidate receive?
options: A percentage score and a rank against other candidates
Only that they passed — no numeric score
The exact number of questions answered correctly
A curved letter grade
quiz.explanation: Since scores are equated, a passing candidate sees only 'Pass' with no number. Only a failing candidate gets an equated score plus a by-Function diagnostic profile to build a retake plan from.

quiz.stem: Which statement about sitting the Series 7 versus the SIE is TRUE?
options: Both exams require sponsorship by a FINRA member firm
The Series 7 requires firm sponsorship via Form U4; the SIE does not require a sponsor
The SIE requires a sponsor but the Series 7 does not
Neither exam requires a sponsor as long as you are over 18
quiz.explanation: The Series 7 is a job license: a member firm must sponsor you by filing Form U4, which opens a 120-day window. The SIE needs no sponsor and can be taken at 18 — which is why candidates take it first.

quiz.stem: An equated passing score of 72 means that:
options: Every candidate must answer exactly 72% of the questions correctly
Scores are adjusted across forms so difficulty differences do not help or hurt a candidate
72 candidates out of 100 will pass on any given day
The exam is graded on a curve relative to the day's other test-takers
quiz.explanation: Equating places different item sets on a common scale so a harder form does not penalize you; the passing bar is an absolute standard, not a curve against other candidates. That is why raw '72% = 90/125' is only an approximation.

quiz.stem: How long does an SIE pass remain valid, and what opens the 120-day exam window for the Series 7?
options: SIE valid 2 years; window opens when the SIE is passed
SIE valid 4 years; window opens when the firm files Form U4
SIE valid 4 years; window opens when the candidate turns 18
SIE valid 5 years; window opens when CE is completed
quiz.explanation: The SIE stays valid 4 years from the pass date. The Series 7 enrollment window (120 days) opens when the sponsoring firm's Form U4 request is processed in CRD; it does not open by passing the SIE or by age.

quiz.stem: A Series 7 question reads: 'All of the following are true EXCEPT…'. What is the item asking you to identify?
options: The most correct of four true statements
The single statement that is false
Two statements that are both true
The statement that is true only in a margin account
quiz.explanation: An EXCEPT (or NOT) stem inverts the task: three options are true and you select the one that is false. Spotting the polarity word before reading the options is the first step of the stem-reading protocol; missing it flips your answer.
